newsitem.title: UK: Thai government to buy 100,000 T rubber May-July.
newsitem.headline: Thai government to buy 100,000 T rubber May-July.

text.p: The Thai government plans to buy 100,000 tonnes of unsmoked sheet rubber between May and July under the country's latest market intervention programme, a Thai official said on Friday.

Sucharit Promdej, a senior adviser at the Department of Agriculture, told Reuters Bangkok was also exploring the possibility of bartering its rubber and other commodities for Chinese fertiliser and heavy machinery.
This follows market talk, later dismissed by Thai traders and rubber authorities, that China might buy 80,000 tonnes of Thai benchmark ribbed smoked sheet (RSS3) rubber for second half 1997 delivery.
Sucharit is attending a two-day international rubber forum which ends on Friday.
Detailing the government's market intervention role, he said, "The government has targeted some 100,000 tonnes for the intervention."
The bulk of the rubber would be unsmoked sheet three rubber (USS3) and the rest lower quality USS4.
The government said on May 13 that it has reserved 4.7 billion baht to buy rubber from planters from May 15 to July 31.
The cabinet has also approved new intervention prices of 29 baht a kg for USS3 and 25 baht for USS4. The previous USS3 intervention price had been 27.5 baht. There used to be no USS4 buying price.
On May 2, the government signed a memorandum of understanding with disgruntled growers in the major growing provinces in the south, promising that it would raise intervention prices.
Another Thai official said last week that the government has spent 170 million baht buying 5,770 tonnes of rubber.
Chakant Saengraksawong, the director of the Hat Yai rubber auction market, said the government expected to spend only one billion baht of the 4.7 billion baht earmarked for price support.
Sucharit added, "Rubber prices have been falling since early this year but the cost of production is rising."
The government price for USS3 of 29 baht was much higher than the market price of 24 baht. "But we have to do something to help the farmers," he said.
Sucharit also said a Thai rubber futures exchange would be established by next year.

Thailand currently relies on the Japanese and Singapore futures markets, two of the world's active rubber exchanges. But Sucharit said the the Japanese market was too speculative while Singapore futures were dominated by three or four big tyre firms.
